origin.description: Set the default encoding and return the previous friendly name.

arguments.name: enc
arguments.text: One encoding name. NA and an empty string are errors.

origin.details: This ICU is built with U_CHARSET_IS_UTF8, so the request does not change the default. The function still warns and prints the short settings line. The returned name is the previous friendly name. The call is process-wide when the charset is not locked, so a caller that changes it sets the previous name again.
origin.value: A single string, the previous friendly name.
origin.example:
previous <- stri_enc_set("ISO-8859-2")
stri_enc_set(previous)
cat(paste0("stri_enc_set(\"ISO-8859-2\") returns ", previous, " because this ICU build keeps the default charset locked.\n"))

translation.description: Set the default encoding and return the previous friendly name.

arguments.name: enc
arguments.text: One encoding name. NA and an empty string are errors.

translation.details: This ICU is built with U_CHARSET_IS_UTF8, so the request does not change the default. The function still warns and prints the short settings line to stderr. The timed proof sets ISO-8859-2, reads the default, and sets the previous name again. Both names are UTF-8.
translation.example:
from stringi.encoding import stri_enc_set
import warnings
with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
    previous = stri_enc_set("ISO-8859-2")
    stri_enc_set(previous)
print(f"stri_enc_set(\"ISO-8859-2\") returns {previous} because this ICU build keeps the default charset locked.")
